# blendops-glb-budget

Purpose: Set and check polycount, texture, and file-size budgets for GLB delivery on web and mobile.

Metadata: Contract `v2.0.0` | Category `quality-validators` | Role `glb-polycount-texture-and-mobile-budget` | Tier `L0` | Runtime default `Not Run` | Artifact default `Not Produced` | Mutation `downgrade_only`

## When to use & trigger cues
- A GLB is going to web or mobile.
- Polycount, texture size, or file size needs a budget or check.
- Trigger phrases: "what's a good polycount for mobile", "how big can the GLB be", "will this load on iPhone", "what should I aim for on a phone", "is the polycount okay", "check triangle budget", "what's blowing the budget", "topology issue?"

## When not to use (delegation boundaries)
- offline pre-rendered video (no real-time budget needed) → use `blendops-lighting-materials` (`references/skill-blendops-lighting-materials.md`; no real-time budget needed)
- replacing engineering load testing (this skill sets a planning budget, not a real-world benchmark) → use `blendops-glb-web-handoff` (`references/skill-blendops-glb-web-handoff.md`; this skill sets a planning budget, not a real-world benchmark)
- material validation → use `blendops-lighting-materials` (`references/skill-blendops-lighting-materials.md`; use blendops-lighting-materials)
- lighting validation → use `blendops-lighting-materials` (`references/skill-blendops-lighting-materials.md`; use blendops-lighting-materials)
- composition validation → use `blendops-camera` (`references/skill-blendops-camera.md`; use blendops-camera)
- broad scene readiness review → use `blendops-final-check` (`references/skill-blendops-final-check.md`; use blendops-final-check)
- classifying render or export artifact evidence → use `blendops-final-check` (`references/skill-blendops-final-check.md`; use blendops-final-check)

## Input & output contract
- Required input `target_device_tier_and_network` (`string`): Target mobile/web hardware tier (iOS Safari, mid-range Android, desktop WebGL) and load budget
- Required input `scene_deliverable_type` (`string`): Whether the GLB is a single hero product, multi-item configurator, or animated character
- Optional input `compression_pipeline_support` (`object`): Whether the host app supports Draco, Meshopt, or KTX2 BasisU transcoding
- Optional input `scene_geometry_inventory` (`array`): Per-object triangle, vertex, modifier stack, and subdivision level counts
- Optional input `pinned_geometry_budget` (`object`): Target triangle and draw-call ceilings from blendops-glb-budget or brief
- Optional input `deformation_or_rig_requirements` (`object`): Optional skeletal deformation or silhouette curvature constraints
- Output contract: `pinned_glb_performance_budget_table`, `triangle_drawcall_and_texture_ceilings`, `compression_and_lod_requirements`, `polycount_and_topology_verdict_table`, `top_budget_offenders_ranking`, `decimation_or_retopology_remediation_plan` (Runtime status: `Not Run`, Artifact status: `Not Produced`, `downgrade_only`).

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- Runtime boundary: BlendOps runtime guidance uses **2 MCP execution paths plus a CLI fallback appendix** (replaces older 3-stack and 4-route drafts — see `docs/runtime-stack-strategy.md` for the corrected attribution history):
- Does not install Blender, configure an MCP bridge, or own a runtime; it points to upstream paths only.
- Does not claim render, export, preview, or GLB results without evidence.
- Does not hand the user Python as the final interface.
